segments.text: In the present situation, a South Indian Federation—that is, the establishment of Dravidian land as a separate country—is possible! Not merely possible, but necessary too.

blocks.text: In the present situation, a South Indian Federation—that is, the establishment of Dravidian land as a separate country—is possible! Not merely possible, but necessary too.

segments.text: Only then will there be a way—and the means—for the many rare and great resources in South India to benefit South Indians themselves, the Dravidians themselves.

segments.text: Seeing, in so many ways, those at the Centre trying to strengthen themselves and the provinces striving to obtain their respective rights, we—the Dravidians of the South—must have no difference of opinion that our country must become a separate country; if there is such a difference, we must wipe it out!

segments.text: Those who belittle our agitation, our struggle, must either be people who do not know us well, or people who know us and yet have descended into mischief.

segments.text: Should not the friends who boast of having driven out the white man who enslaved the Indian land and ruled it in a lust for power know this?

segments.text: Knowing that domination, arrogance, police, armies and press power are not permanent, why this obstinacy?

segments.text: To smash the arrogant man's obstinacy; to make our province (Dravidian country) live in complete freedom; to keep unwanted Hindi from entering; to enjoy our own wealth; to break the iron capitalist doctrine of the North that Birla or Bajaj or Tata or Dalmia nurture under the cloak of nationalism; to make way for equality; to obtain a joyous Dravidian land—raise the heroic cry: ‘Kaamaarkkung kudiyallom!’ ‘Dravidian land for the Dravidians!’
